newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Proton six-mth profits seen up.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Proton six-mth profits seen up.

text.p: Malaysian car maker Perusahaan Otomobil Nasional Bhd (Proton) is expected to report higher first-half profits when it releases its results this week, analysts said on Monday.

Proton's results for six months ended September 30, 1996 could be released any time between a board meeting on November 27 and the end of the month, sources close to the company told Reuters on Monday.
Analysts have been expecting bullish news from the automaker and said they maintained their projections for interim pre-tax profits to be around 450 million ringgit.

Proton's group pre-tax profit for the six months to September 30, 1995 was 127.3 million ringgit, while the group's pre-tax profit for the financial year to March 31, 1996 totalled 454.6 million ringgit.

Analysts told Reuters in October that the expected sharp rise in earnings would be due to a weaker Japanese yen during the period, and lower production costs brought about by reduced costs on locally-made components.
"There have been no changes in our estimates of the interim results since last month," said Choo Swee Kee, motor analyst at research house Vickers Ballas on Monday.
The acquisition of an 80 percent stake in British car maker Group Lotus Ltd would not affect the interim results since it took place after September 30, analysts said.
